Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
- 65-year-old male with acute central chest pressure, nausea, diaphoresis, dyspnea, and left arm/shoulder pain; emergency services activated for possible acute coronary syndrome.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Central “pressure” chest discomfort began while gardening ~2 hours ago; still present.
- Associated symptoms: Nausea (no vomiting), diaphoresis, shortness of breath, palpitations, pain radiating to left arm and shoulder.
- Pertinent negatives: First episode; no previous similar pain.
- Past medical history: Hypertension. No diabetes. Cholesterol status unknown.
- Allergies: Aspirin – mild allergic swelling (not life-threatening).
- Medications: Not documented.
- Family history: Father died of myocardial infarction at ~60 y; mother with heart disease.
- Social history: Smokes ~10 cigarettes/day x 15 yrs; drinks ~7–8 pints beer/week; overweight; low exercise; lives alone; restaurant owner.

Examination:
- Vitals: Not available.
- Physical findings: None documented (video consult).

Impression:
- Suspected acute coronary syndrome / myocardial infarction.

Plan:
- Emergency plan: Ambulance summoned; physician remained on call until arrival.
- ED/hospital: Paramedics to perform ECG and transport to appropriate facility.
- Patient instructed to keep front door open for access.
- Allergy communication: Patient reminded to inform EMS/ED of aspirin allergy; clinician to hand over details.
- Possible aspirin use to be weighed despite mild allergy (risk/benefit to be assessed in hospital).

Quality checks:

● Missing/expected elements:
  – Current medications list.
  – Baseline vitals, physical exam, ECG, cardiac biomarkers.
  – Complete allergy list beyond aspirin.
  – Formal medication reconciliation and past surgical history.

● Internal conflicts:
  – Age discrepancy: DOB 08/08/1958 (would be 65 y) vs. patient/doctor estimating “around 60”/“51” (minor calculation error).

● Transcript quality: Clear; minimal background noise; no inaudible sections.
